title: What does an AI-assisted game asset pipeline actually cost? Here's my honest breakdown
author: Akami-Assets
selftext:
Making game icons with AI sounds cheap until you actually price the stack.

I've been building a casual mobile icon pack catalog for a few months - potions, creatures, status effects, UI elements, that kind of thing. Thick line art, soft gradients, cozy style. The kind of assets that need to look consistent across 30-60 icons per pack.

Here's what my monthly bill actually looks like.

**Photoshop - non-negotiable**

Post-processing, export, compositing preview sheets. I haven't found anything at this quality level that fits my workflow. Stays.

**ChatGPT ImageToImage - core generation**

This is where most assets start. Rough generation, then I correct in Photoshop. It's not perfect but it's fast and the results are controllable enough for icon work.

**Layer AI - the expensive one**

I have a LoRA trained on my style there. Useful for consistency when an icon needs several rounds of correction -it keeps things on-model without manual rework each time. It works. It's also the biggest line item.

The plan is to migrate to ComfyUI and retrain the LoRA locally. ComfyUI is free, runs offline, and does the same job. I'm keeping Layer AI until I have time to set up the pipeline properly- a rushed migration costs more time than the subscription.

**Things I'm also looking at:** Pixel Lab and Ludo AI are on my list to test. Ludo in particular has asset-specific features - trend analysis, concept generation - that might be useful for planning new packs before I start generating. Haven't tried them in production yet.

**Claude Code - the one that's hard to quantify**

File organization, batch operations, table work, archive management. Technically I could do all of this manually. But "technically possible manually" and "actually sustainable at 1 pack per week" are different things. This one stays.

**Total: roughly €75/month**

Current sales: not proportional to that number yet. This isn't my main income - it's a parallel project I'm building seriously. So I think of it as infrastructure investment, not operational cost. But I'm not going to ignore the gap forever. The goal is to get tooling to pay for itself. The Layer AI → ComfyUI migration is the main lever. Everything else stays until something better becomes obvious.

**If you're running an AI-assisted asset pipeline - what does your stack look like? Especially curious if anyone has already made the Layer AI → ComfyUI switch and what the setup time actually was.**
